# SEO-460: Exclude untranslated pages from the locale cluster

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| --- | --- |

| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

A locale route that returns source-language text because no translation exists is left out of the annotation set, so the cluster describes only the pages actually rendered in the language they claim.

## Rationale

A route that answers in the wrong language while declaring another one misdescribes itself, and a reader who follows the declaration arrives at text they cannot read.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site",
    "multilingual"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Have the translation layer report which locales a given page exists in, and build the annotation set from that report rather than from the list of locales the site supports overall.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Compare the rendered body language of each annotated locale route against the language it declares and report routes where the two disagree.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `ROUTE`, `VALIDATOR_OUTPUT`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: This asserts only that a declaration should match what the route returns, which is an internal consistency property needing no external citation. Whether a partial translation is worth publishing is an editorial decision left to the site.
